perspective:
Jose Castillo’s available information:

- He works with Patricia Ndiaye at a community bank, where he sometimes helps with maintenance and repairs. They have a friendly, professional relationship and usually chat about everyday work experiences.
- He noticed Patricia seemed more withdrawn than usual and remembered her as usually vibrant.
- He asked if she was okay. She said it was “nothing really,” just “some personal stuff,” and thanked him for asking.
- He offered to listen if she ever wanted to talk. She said she appreciated it and that it meant a lot.
- Later, during a lunch break, he overheard Patricia on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments.
- He told her managing finances can be stressful, mentioned he had been reading about financial planning strategies, and offered to discuss them with her.
- She said that could be helpful and that she’d been overwhelmed with her bills lately.
- He offered to look over budgeting tips together and said she could let him know when she felt up to it. She thanked him and said she’d take him up on it soon.
- Afterward, he worried he might have overstepped by bringing up finances.
- He asked Patricia if she minded, explaining he wanted to help, not pry. She said she didn’t think he was prying and was grateful for his offer.
- He told her he was relieved, respected her privacy, and wanted to support her as a friend. She said she appreciated that and was glad she had someone to turn to.
- Later, he checked in with her by asking about her weekend. She said she was fine and planned a quiet weekend at home. He said he planned to read and relax, and reminded her he was available if she needed anything.
- He continued to check in with her at work. She said she was busy but handling it, and thanked him for checking in. He offered help with anything, even just getting coffee. She said she would let him know and appreciated his support.
